SECTION 1 CORPORATE PROFILE

1.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Nov 02, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation announces share split

Southern Copper Corporation has announced a 1 for 1.01 share split, on Tuesday, November 03. The shares last traded at $179.36.

Press Release article 2 of 8, Source: SOUTHERN COPPER CORP/, 330 words

Oct 21, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE and BVL: SCCO)

Exhibit 99.1

Victor Pedraglio

Bertin Galarreta

Adjusted EBITDA in 9M26 was $8,609.0 million, 56.2% higher than in 9M25. The adjusted EBITDA margin in 9M26 stood at 65.0% versus 57.7% in 9M25.

On a YTD basis, copper production fell 2.9% in 2026 to stand at 693,602 tonnes. This evolution was mainly driven by a decrease in production at our Peruvian mines due to lower ore grades. YoY the Company smelting and refining facilities increased their production by 15.8% and 10.1%, respectively.

On a YTD basis, mined silver production rose 1.5% compared to 2025. Zinc and molybdenum production were down 7.2% and 5.2% in 2026, respectively.

In 9M26, the operating cash cost per pound of copper, net of by-product revenue credits, was $0.01. This represents a decrease of 98.1% compared to the $0.61 reported in 9M25. The 9M26 cash cost decrease was driven by an increase in by-product revenue credits (+53.6%).

In lieu of fractional shares, cash will be distributed to each shareholder who would otherwise have been entitled to receive a fractional share, based on a share price of $197.83, which is the average of the high and low share price on October 15, 2026.

Mr. German Larrea, Chairman of the Board, commenting on the Companys progress and current circumstances, said: "We are very pleased with our strong third-quarter performance, which delivered a record for net sales, adjusted EBITDA and net income. These achievements were thanks to our strategy and disciplined cost control at the operational level.

Our Tia Maria project is reaching half completion this month, and significant goals have been achieved on different construction fronts. As planned, we have finished pre-stripping works at the La Tapada deposit to uncover areas where mineral can be extracted when we begin operations. Simultaneously, work in the dry and wet areas, where most of the solvent extraction and electrowinning activities will be performed, is advancing steadily and according to projected timelines.

Wireless is the principal revenue source, with 332 million wireless lines at quarter-end, including 153 million postpaid customers, alongside 80 million fixed-line RGUs. Brazil is the largest wireless market at 92.8 million subscribers, followed by Mexico at 81.8 million. BRAZILIAN MARKET REPORT

Monthly: Desktop Sigmanet Comunicacao Multimidia SA (SA:DESK3) decreases on below average volume [Ranked 1]

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 11th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Dec 04, 2025: ASUR Calls for a Shareholders' Meeting

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. The following is the complete text of the call to assembly for the shareholders' meeting: CALL TO ASSEMBLY FOR ORDINARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF GRUPO AEROPORTUARIO DEL SURESTE, S.A.B. DE C.V. By resolution of the Board of Directors adopted at the meeting held on the September 30th 2025 and pursuant to the provisions of Articles 36, 37 and other provisions of the bylaws of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (the "Company") and Articles 181 and 183 of the General Corporations Law ("Ley General de Sociedades Mercantiles"), the Company's shareholders are hereby called to attend the Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting (the "Meeting"), which will take place at 10 o'clock a.m. on the 26 th of January 2026, at the Company's offices at Bosque de Alisos No. 47-A 4 th floor, Colonia Bosque de las Lomas, 05120, Mexico City, Mexico, in order to discuss the following matters: A G E N D A I. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to acquire all or part of the shares and/or airport operators, including Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes, either directly or through its subsidiaries and/or special purpose vehicles. Resolutions thereon. II. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to, directly or indirectly, contract any type of debt, either through bank loans, securities issuances, or any other form of financing, and to enter into the contracts and agreements necessary and/or convenient to implement the foregoing.

Press Release article 3 of 3, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The company's recent financial metrics reveal total revenue of approximately MXN 292.5 billion, operating income of about MXN 40.4 billion, and a net income of roughly MXN 23.0 billion. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. With an Acquirer's Multiple of 4.0 and robust operating margins, the company appears to be a promising long-term investment for value-seeking investors looking at the consumer staples sector.

Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Recent News 4 of 6, Source: HourlyBusinessNews

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. 8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Recent News 3 of 4, Source: HourlyBusinessNews

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Jun 09, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Publishes its 2025 Sustainability Report

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 08, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces the publication of its2025 Sustainability Report, which presents the Companys performance, progress, and key initiatives related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters during 2025.

The report covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025, and was prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards and the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) framework. In addition, it incorporates considerations aligned with other international reporting frameworks, including IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2, issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB).

The full report is available on GAPs website at www.aeropuertosgap.com.mx under the Investors section.

Company Description

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) operates 12 airports throughout Mexicos Pacific region, including the major cities of Guadalajara and Tijuana, the four tourist destinations of Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos, La Paz and Manzanillo, and six other mid-sized cities: Hermosillo, Guanajuato, Morelia, Aguascalientes, Mexicali, and Los Mochis. In February 2006, GAPs shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol PAC and on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol GAP. In April 2015, GAP acquired 100% of Desarrollo de Concessioner Aeroportuarias, S.L., which owns a majority stake in MBJ Airports Limited, a company operating Sangster International Airport in Montego Bay, Jamaica. In October 2018, GAP entered into a concession agreement for the Norman Manley International Airport operation in Kingston, Jamaica, and took control of the operation in October 2019.

In accordance with Section 806 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and Article 42 of the Ley del Mercado de Valores, GAP has implemented a whistleblower program, which allows complainants to anonymously and confidentially report suspected activities that involve criminal conduct or violations.

Jun 05, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Reports a Passenger Traffic Decrease in May 2026 of 4.1% Compared to 2025

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 05, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces preliminary terminal passenger traffic figures for May 2026, compared with May 2025.

During May 2026, the 12 Mexican airports operated by GAP recorded a 2.8% decrease in total passenger traffic compared to May 2025. Guadalajara airport reported an increase of 7.1%, while Puerto Vallarta, Tijuana and Los Cabos reported a decrease of 14.4%, 9.8%, and 6.0%, respectively, compared to May 2025. With respect to GAPs airports in Jamaica, Montego Bay recorded a decrease of 19.1%, while Montego Bay recorded a decrease of 5.2%.

*Passengers in Tijuana who use CBX in both directions are classified as international.

The seats available during May 2026 decreased by 7.5%, compared to May 2025. The load factors for the month went from 81.1% in May 2025 to 84.1% in May 2026.

Sep 11, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Secures Ps. 8 Billion Credit for Growth

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (MX:GAPB) has secured a significant financial boost with bank credit lines totaling Ps. 8,000 million from a consortium of prominent lenders, including Santander, BBVA, HSBC, J.P. Morgan, and Scotiabank. On 14th September 2026, the company announced that these short-term facilities, which have terms ranging from 6 to 12 months and feature a floating rate linked to TIIE de Fondeo plus a modest spread, will provide the necessary liquidity at a relatively low cost.

Of the total financing, approximately Ps. 4,258 million is earmarked for refinancing debt securities that are set to mature in September and October 2026. This strategic move is expected to mitigate rollover risk for Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, ensuring the company maintains a stable financial footing as it navigates its obligations. The remaining Ps. 3,742 million will be allocated to capital investments under its Master Development Program for Mexican airports, which is crucial for ongoing infrastructure expansion and enhancing the company's competitive stance in the regional airport sector.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico operates twelve airports across Mexico's Pacific region, serving major urban centers such as Guadalajara and Tijuana, as well as key tourist destinations like Puerto Vallarta and Los Cabos. Additionally, the company manages Sangster International Airport in Montego Bay and Norman Manley International Airport in Kingston, further solidifying its presence in Jamaica's aviation market.

The recent analyst consensus on Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico stock remains positive, with a rating of 'Buy' and a price target of Ps. 520.00. This optimistic outlook is backed by the company's strategic initiatives and its focus on infrastructure development, which are anticipated to bolster growth and profitability in the coming years.

Investors looking for comprehensive insights into Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico's financial health and market position can explore detailed analyses available through various financial platforms. As the company advances its Master Development Program and refines its debt structure, it remains poised to capitalize on growth opportunities in the competitive airport industry.

Recent News 2 of 2, Source: HourlyBusinessNews

Jun 01, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Completes Full Acquisition of Cross Border Xpress

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) has successfully finalized its acquisition of Cross Border Xpress, marking a significant milestone in its expansion strategy. The completion of this transaction was officially recorded on 3rd June 2026, following the notarization of a merger agreement that was initially signed on 30th April 2026.

The acquisition involved GAP purchasing the remaining 25 percent stake in Cross Border Xpress, thereby securing full ownership of the facility. This strategic move not only grants GAP complete control over future earnings but also enhances its operational capabilities in the region. Cross Border Xpress operates a unique pedestrian bridge linking a terminal in San Diego, California, directly to Tijuana International Airport, offering a seamless transit experience for ticketed passengers.

By bypassing traditional border crossing queues, the high-traffic facility generates significant revenue, further complementing Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico's existing airport operations in Tijuana. As a leading airport operator, GAP manages 12 airports across Mexico's Pacific region, serving multiple cities and popular tourist destinations. This acquisition aligns with GAP's strategy to bolster its position in the aviation sector.

In addition to its core aeronautical services, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico diversifies its revenue streams through non-aeronautical activities, which include commercial services such as car parking, shops, hotels, and restaurants. The acquisition of Cross Border Xpress is expected to enhance these non-aeronautical revenue opportunities, with potential expansions in food and beverage services and VIP lounges anticipated.

Overall, the full acquisition of Cross Border Xpress represents a significant growth opportunity for Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, allowing the company to maximize its operational synergies and enhance its service offerings in the highly competitive airport management sector.

ADRS AND DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.36; a deterioration from 0.35 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.18; steady from 0.18 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Altman-Z score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores a Z = 1.23 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.24 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Beneish M-score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Beneish M-score is calculated by using 8 key metrics:

Days Sales in Receivables Index

Gross Margin Index

Asset Quality Index

Sales Growth Index

Depreciation Index

Sales General and Administrative Expenses Index

Leverage Index

Total Accruals to Total Assets Index

Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de has a Beneish M-Score of -4.77 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]. An M-score of less than -1.78 is considered normal. However an M-score greater than -1.78 suggests there could be modifications to its earnings that have occurred to help window dress the headline earnings. Currently about 15 International Depository Receipts companies have a Beneish M-score greater than -1.78.

Piotroski F-Score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 5 for the half year-ended 30 June 2025 indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores an O = -9.845

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

The probability of bankruptcy within one year is given by the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution(X).

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

Algunos gigantes del sector de consumo y retail como la restaurantera Alsea , el conglomerado Fomento Económico Mexicano (FEMSA) y Walmart de México estiman que el aumento al salario mínimo del próximo año rondará entre 12% y 13% en México, cuando también tendrán que reducir de manera gradual la jornada laboral para llegar a las 40 horas al cierre de la década, algo en lo que ya se preparan.

Obviamente, sabíamos que esto iba a suceder. En los últimos años, hemos tenido aumentos de dos dígitos en el salario mínimo. Y ahora, para 2027, no habrá cambios. Prevemos un aumento del 12% en el salario mínimo, además de la reducción de las horas de trabajo semanales", dijo Christian Gurría, director general de Alsea, en llamada trimestral con analistas.

Al mismo tiempo, el directivo compartió que la operadora de las cafeterías Starbucks y de Domino´s Pizza en el país se adelantó para trabajar con seis meses de anticipación en la implementación de la reducción de horas de trabajo.

Hacia la jornada laboral de 40 horas

En general, las empresas deberán disminuir gradualmente la jornada laboral a partir de 2027, con una reducción de dos horas por año, donde cada ajuste se hará efectivo el primer día de cada año.

Es decir, el próximo año la jornada se reducirá a 46 horas semanales; en 2028 a 44; en 2029 a 42; y en 2030 llegaría a las 40 horas , de acuerdo con la Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social.

Dicho esto, aplicaremos la misma estrategia el próximo año. Reduciremos las dos horas restantes en la segunda mitad de 2027 de forma progresiva. Es cierto que, en algún punto, la productividad puede llegar a su límite", agregó Gurría Dubernard.

Para Alsea, la situación depende de cada marca , pues algunas todavía tienen margen de mejora en productividad, mientras que en otras compensan el impacto mediante la implementación de eficiencias adicionales.

Walmart se alista ante cambios laborales

Cristian Barrientos Pozo, presidente y director general de Walmart de México y Centroamérica, también coincidió en que el incremento al salario mínimo podría ir en el mismo rango de 12% para el próximo año.

Nuestros costos operativos aumentan cada año. Esperamos que el salario mínimo crezca alrededor del 12% el próximo año. Como saben, nos enfrentaremos a la reforma laboral, que implica pasar de 48 a 40 horas, comenzando el próximo año con 46″, señaló en la conferencia de resultados financieros de la minorista.

Al respecto, la empresa de supermercados, que tiene 3,389 tiendas en México, trabaja con un equipo global para implementar iniciativas y así estar preparados ante los cambios laborales en el país.

FEMSA ve aumento en gastos laborales

Por su parte, FEMSA, dueña de las tiendas de conveniencia OXXO y la embotelladora Coca-Cola FEMSA , señaló que el aumento en el salario mínimo sería de 13%, lo cual, junto con la reducción de las horas trabajadas, se reflejaría en sus gastos de venta.

En el contexto de salarios que superan con creces la inflación y la próxima reforma laboral que contempla la reducción de la jornada laboral, la eficiencia en los gastos sigue siendo fundamental para la gestión de OXXO, y nos esforzamos constantemente por encontrar nuevas formas de optimizar el gasto", dijo José Antonio Fernández Garza-Lagüera, director general de FEMSA, en la llamada con analistas por los resultados financieros trimestrales del conglomerado.

Martín Arias, director administrativo y de finanzas, señaló que continuarán viendo un aumento en los gastos laborales como porcentaje de los ingresos , probablemente a corto plazo.

Ante ese panorama, FEMSA busca estrategias, incluso dejó abierta la posibilidad deusar robots para atender las tiendas una o dos horas, mientras los trabajadores están enfocados en otras tareas, dado que sus sucursales operan 24 horas al día.

Pero la presión continuará. Esta es una política declarada del gobierno, y todos los minoristas y empresas de consumo tendremos que reaccionar en consecuencia, buscando el equilibrio entre los costos y el precio de venta", indicó Arias.

Aumento de precios de Kimberly-Clark de México ante gastos laborales

Por otra parte, Pablo González Guajardo, director general Kimberly-Clark de México, señaló en pasada llamada trimestral con analistas de la empresa que en general el aumento en costos laborales ha sido un constante "viento en contra" y lo seguirá siendo con la transición a las 40 horas.

En lo particular, la empresa que comercializa productos como Kleenex no solo se enfrenta al aumento en costos por factores laborales, sino también por las materias primas y el transporte, además de una demanda débil.

Por ello, la empresa contempla ajustar sus precios , aunque sin aplicar un porcentaje fijo a todos los productos, sino que analizarán cada categoría.

Mientras tanto, diversas empresas en México tendrán que adaptarse a la nueva jornada laboral.

Grupo México, GCC, and Megacable are among the companies listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) that are exploring acquisition opportunities to expand their businesses, as revealed during the financial reporting season for the third quarter of 2026.

Chedraui, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP), Arca Continental, and Alpek are also assessing growth opportunities through the acquisition of companies or assets, although some condition possible operations on their financial situation and investment priorities.

Among the issuers, Grupo México stands out, a conglomerate controlled by Germán Larrea , which is seeking growth opportunities across its three business divisions: mining, transportation, and infrastructure.

"We aim to grow within our three business lines and are evaluating opportunities that will ensure sustained growth and value creation," explained Marlene Finny, the company's Chief Financial Officer, during a call with analysts and investors.

The group reported an cash position of $13.79 billion at the end of the third quarter, compared to $9.64 billion recorded in the same period of 2025, representing a 43% increase.

Additionally, at the end of November, it will pay its first dividend entirely in shares since July 2009 , a measure that will allow it to preserve cash resources and have greater financial flexibility.

GCC and Megacable maintain interest in new acquisitions

The cement company GCC allocated $104 million for acquisitions during the first nine months of 2026 and continues to seek companies to expand its presence in the construction materials business.

The company is focusing its interest on small and medium-sized enterprises in the aggregates segment, materials used in concrete production , although it is also not ruling out opportunities in the cement business, where it has already identified several options.

"We remain optimistic and proactive in pursuing growth opportunities for the company," stated Enrique Escalante, CEO of GCC, during the conference with analysts and investors.

Acquisition strategy will remain among the main priorities of the cement company, according to Maik Strecker, Director of Finance and Planning .

"We have a portfolio of merger and acquisition opportunities. That will remain our top priority," the executive affirmed.

On its part, Megacable is keeping the possibility of acquisitions open in the fixed telecommunications market , although any operation must align with its cash generation objectives and leverage levels.

"We continue to seek to be a strong player in the fixed telecommunications market or identify opportunities to add more value to shareholders," said Raymundo Fernández, Deputy CEO of the company.

The interest in potential acquisitions is not new . Since the second quarter of the year, the company has suggested the possibility of capitalizing on opportunities to strengthen its market position.

However, Enrique Yamuni , CEO of Megacable, made it clear that investment decisions will need to take the company's financial situation and shareholder benefits into account.

"Our priority remains to balance investments that drive future growth with actions that enhance shareholder value," he explained.

Chedraui, GAP, and other issuers are also evaluating opportunities

Grupo Chedraui is not ruling out making acquisitions in the United States long-term, despite the macroeconomic environment and high competition in that country's retail market.

Carlos Smith, Director of Chedraui USA , explained that the company follows a disciplined strategy to evaluate possible operations and seize opportunities that may arise among its competitors.

"In such situations, there are always winners and losers. We are very disciplined in our merger and acquisition strategy… We are always alert to possible opportunities," he stated.

In the airport sector, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP) is also considering new growth opportunities through acquisitions, after incorporating the Cross Border Xpress , the pedestrian bridge connecting Tijuana with San Diego, California, into its operations.

The company aims to leverage the financial benefits of this incorporation to assess future investments that will allow it to expand its operations.

Arca Continental , one of the leading bottlers of Coca-Cola in Latin America , is also continuing to assess potential acquisitions. However, it prioritizes investments in its operations and dividend payments to shareholders.

Lastly, the petrochemical company Alpek is considering growth opportunities through acquisitions, although it first aims to reduce its debt to strengthen its financial flexibility and advance its own project portfolio development.

"We remain optimistic and proactive in pursuing growth opportunities for the company," stated Enrique Escalante, CEO of GCC, during the conference with analysts and investors.

Acquisition strategy will remain among the main priorities of the cement company, according to Maik Strecker, Director of Finance and Planning .

"We have a portfolio of merger and acquisition opportunities. That will remain our top priority," the executive affirmed.

On its part, Megacable is keeping the possibility of acquisitions open in the fixed telecommunications market , although any operation must align with its cash generation objectives and leverage levels.

"We continue to seek to be a strong player in the fixed telecommunications market or identify opportunities to add more value to shareholders," said Raymundo Fernández, Deputy CEO of the company.

The interest in potential acquisitions is not new . Since the second quarter of the year, the company has suggested the possibility of capitalizing on opportunities to strengthen its market position.

However, Enrique Yamuni , CEO of Megacable, made it clear that investment decisions will need to take the company's financial situation and shareholder benefits into account.

"Our priority remains to balance investments that drive future growth with actions that enhance shareholder value," he explained.

Chedraui, GAP, and other issuers are also evaluating opportunities

Grupo Chedraui is not ruling out making acquisitions in the United States long-term, despite the macroeconomic environment and high competition in that country's retail market.

Carlos Smith, Director of Chedraui USA , explained that the company follows a disciplined strategy to evaluate possible operations and seize opportunities that may arise among its competitors.

"In such situations, there are always winners and losers. We are very disciplined in our merger and acquisition strategy… We are always alert to possible opportunities," he stated.

In the airport sector, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP) is also considering new growth opportunities through acquisitions, after incorporating the Cross Border Xpress , the pedestrian bridge connecting Tijuana with San Diego, California, into its operations.

The company aims to leverage the financial benefits of this incorporation to assess future investments that will allow it to expand its operations.

Arca Continental , one of the leading bottlers of Coca-Cola in Latin America , is also continuing to assess potential acquisitions. However, it prioritizes investments in its operations and dividend payments to shareholders.

Lastly, the petrochemical company Alpek is considering growth opportunities through acquisitions, although it first aims to reduce its debt to strengthen its financial flexibility and advance its own project portfolio development.

Walmart de México y Centroamérica has promoted an injunction against regulations related to the application of the Seating Law , arguing that some of the obligations set forth by the Ministry of Labor and Social Welfare (STPS) exceed what is prescribed in the Federal Labor Law and represent excessive and unnecessary costs for businesses.

The case reached the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation (SCJN) , which was scheduled to discuss it on November 5. However, the matter was removed from the agenda before the session began, leaving its resolution pending.

In its injunction request, filed on August 27, 2025, Walmart claimed that the administrative provisions go beyond the obligation to provide seats or chairs with backs for workers , whether for performing their activities or for periodic rest during the workday.

The regulations extend beyond merely regulating aspects related to the reform of the Federal Labor Law regarding the obligation to provide a sufficient number of seats or chairs with backs to all workers when the nature of the work allows, for carrying out their functions or for periodic rest during the workday," argued the company.

The supermarket chain also challenged measures such as the use of ergonomic footwear, the conditioning of floors in workstations, and the requirement to maintain records of verification walks , as it considers them to impose additional costs that it deems excessive and unnecessary.

These do not relate to the reform of the Federal Labor Law concerning the provision of seats for workers. Furthermore, the measures contradict other regulations that govern safety in workplaces," Walmart stated.

Supreme Court holds Walmart's injunction in abeyance

The litigation, identified at the SCJN as injunction under review 260/2026 , reached the highest court after a district judge denied the protection sought by the requesting companies, who challenged this initial ruling.

The project drafted by Minister Arístides Rodrigo Guerrero García proposes to return the case file to the Sixteenth Collegiate Labor Court of the First Circuit , considering that it is that body's responsibility to resolve the controversy regarding the administrative provisions.

It is appropriate to return the matter to the Sixteenth Collegiate Labor Court of the First Circuit (…), because, although a constitutional issue persists, it pertains to a provision of general observance whose knowledge was delegated to the Circuit Collegiate Courts," the draft states.

If approved in these terms, the Supreme Court would not resolve the substance of the arguments presented by Walmart , but rather return the case file to the Collegiate Court for further analysis.

However, the removal of the matter from the session on November 5 left the discussion of the project pending, with no new date confirmed for its consideration.

What does the Seating Law establish?

The so-called Seating Law , which came into effect in June 2025, amended the Federal Labor Law to require companies in the commercial and service sectors, among other workplaces included in the legislation, to provide sufficient seats or chairs with backs to their employees.

The reform also prohibits employers from requiring workers to stand throughout their entire workday without allowing them to sit periodically .

Subsequently, the STPS published provisions to regulate its implementation, which include the identification of risks associated with standing for prolonged periods, as well as preventive measures to protect the health of workers.

These obligations gave rise to the judicial controversy , as Walmart considers that some of the measures exceed what is established in the labor reform.

Walmart anticipates higher labor costs in Mexico

The litigation occurs while Walmart de México y Centroamérica faces additional pressures on its labor costs due to wage increases and expected changes in Mexican labor legislation.

During its conference with analysts and investors for the third quarter of 2026, Cristian Barrientos, CEO of Walmart de México y Centroamérica , stated that the company is working on measures to prepare for the new labor conditions.

This year, we have been working very closely with a global team to implement many initiatives that will help us be better prepared for this new way of working in Mexico," the executive assured.

Among the factors the company is considering are a possible 12% increase to the minimum wage and the reduction of the workweek to 40 hours .

Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a network of 13 airports primarily in the north-central region, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business activities focus on the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger handling, cargo services, commercial concessions, and real estate development. The company generates revenue through aeronautical fees, such as landing and parking charges, as well as non-aeronautical sources like retail, advertising, and parking. Among its fastest-growing segments are international passenger traffic, fueled by rising tourism and business travel, and cargo operations, which have expanded due to e-commerce and cross-border trade. OMA's strategic investments in modernization and expansion have enhanced operational efficiency, supporting sustained growth in a recovering aviation market. This positions the company as a vital contributor to Mexico's transportation infrastructure and economic connectivity. It is Mexico's 4th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.
